details:
Q1: How should a replacement for an untrusted PR be handled? "Untrusted" means a fork head (`head.repo.full_name` is not this repository) or a PR author that is not OWNER, MEMBER or COLLABORATOR, the pipeline login, or `github-actions[bot]`. Both values come from the `pulls/<n>` response `unblock_judge.sh` already fetches, so no new API call is needed.
Choices:
A) Fail closed at the source. `unblock_judge.sh` passes a `pr_trusted` flag (plus the PR author and head SHA) into the context. For an untrusted PR, `unblock_actions.py` creates no replacement issue: it closes the PR, posts a comment explaining why, and sends a Telegram WARNING. Replacements for trusted PRs get a provenance marker (source PR, author, head repo, head SHA) for audit. `clarify.yml` and the consumer templates do not change. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Still create the replacement issue for an untrusted PR, but give it a hold label (e.g. `ai:needs-human`) and a provenance marker, so the pipeline starts only after a trusted human posts `/reclarify`. This needs the issue-open gate to honour that label at creation time.
C) Persist provenance markers on every replacement issue, and make the issue-open gate in `clarify.yml` (plus `internal-clarify.yml` and `workflow-templates/ai-clarify.yml`) check the marker's source PR and author against GitHub, not just the issue creator. This is wider in scope and touches the consumer-synced gate.
Q2: Should the fix cover every unblock verdict that creates an issue from a PR item, or only `reissue`?
Choices:
A) Every PR-item path that creates an issue from model-derived content: `reissue`, the standalone `descope` and `operator_step` fix-ups (`_fixup_ops`), and `accept_with_followup`. It is the same class of defect. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Only the `reissue` branch named in the finding (`scripts/unblock_actions.py:268`).
